questions.question: What problem does consistent hashing primarily solve?
options: Limiting ownership changes when the node set changes
questions.explanation: Consistent hashing is a placement technique. It keeps most key-to-owner mappings stable when one owner joins or leaves.

questions.question: A key hashes past the largest token on a ring. Which owner receives it?
options: The node with the largest token
The first token after wrapping to the start of the ring
No node until the ring is rebuilt
questions.explanation: Successor lookup wraps around the ordered hash space, so the first token owns the range after the final token.

questions.question: Why can virtual nodes improve balance?
options: They split one physical owner's responsibility into more, smaller ranges
They make hot keys use several owners
questions.explanation: Several token positions let one physical node receive smaller ranges from different parts of the ring. This reduces the effect of a few large random gaps.

questions.question: Three balanced nodes become four equally weighted nodes. About what share of keys tends to move to the new node?
questions.explanation: The new node should own about 1 / (3 + 1) of the balanced key space. A concrete sample can vary, so production systems measure actual movement.

questions.question: A replica walk selects three adjacent tokens, but the first two tokens belong to the same physical machine. How many independent physical copies were selected?
questions.explanation: Two token positions on one machine still represent one physical failure boundary. The third token adds only one more independent node.

questions.question: Which statement about replication factor is correct?
options: It fully defines read and write consistency
It is the requested number of copies, separate from acknowledgement rules
It guarantees copies occupy different zones
It removes the need for repair
questions.explanation: Replication factor describes copy count. Consistency levels, failure-domain placement, repair, and conflict handling are separate contracts.

questions.question: Which production signal most directly exposes stale routing views during membership change?
options: The number of code comments in the client
The compression ratio of stored values
questions.explanation: Versioning the membership map lets the system detect routers that still calculate ownership from an older token set.
